# local 0001: Pointers to int that are initialized with wide string literals get bytes of a host address

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17158
- Recommended action: Fix together with bug #3973, which has the same cause in printIvalPtr.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

`support/regression/tests/p99-conformance.c` defines these two objects.

```c
int const* has_universal_string_4 = L"‘Χ⁠X’";
int const* has_universal_string_8 = L"\U00002018\U000003A7\U00002060X\U00002019";
```

`wchar_t` is `unsigned long` in SDCC, so the type of the pointers and the type of the literals
differ, and the test disables warning 244 for that reason. The regression suite compiles the test
for the large model with `make -C support/regression test-mcs51-large`. On r17158 the assembly
that the compiler writes for the test has three literal bytes as the initial value of each
pointer, where the address of the string belongs.

```
__xinit__has_universal_string_4:
; generic printIvalPtr
	.byte #0x20,#0x8b,#0xad
__xinit__has_universal_string_8:
; generic printIvalPtr
	.byte #0x20,#0x8b,#0xad
```

The bytes change from one run of the compiler to the next. The same build wrote `c0 1c 47` for
mcs51-huge and `90 f3 5f` for mcs51-large-stack-auto. The string itself is emitted in each of the
three variants.

For mcs51-medium the compiler initializes the two pointers by code, and that code loads the
address of the string. The test excludes these objects for the small model.

The two lines were compiled only as part of the test. They were not compiled as a file of their
own.

## Cause

`printIvalPtr` in `src/SDCCglue.c` calls `printIvalCharPtr`, which prints the label of the string,
only when the pointer in the declaration points to a character type or to an unsigned `int` type
of any length. `int const *` is neither. The value that `constExprValue` returns for a string
literal has the storage class `S_LITERAL`, and the numeric members of its union overlap the
compiler's pointer to the characters. `printIvalPtr` therefore executes its `IS_LITERAL` branch,
which prints the low bytes of that pointer with `aopLiteral`.

The functions are shared by the ports. mcs51 was the only port examined.

## Related

Bug #3973 reports this output for a `const void *` object that is initialized with a narrow string
literal. Its test case shows the defect in every mcs51 model, because the object is `const`. The
fix that its entry outlines covers both.
